title: Rinderrouladen
subtitle: German beef rolls stuffed with bacon and mustard
excerpt: Thin slices of beef are spread with mustard, layered with bacon, onion, and capers, then rolled and braised until tender in a rich sauce. This is a beloved German Sunday lunch dish. Regional variations exist across the country, but the rolled, braised format is constant.
sourceNotes: Rouladen are a beloved German Sunday lunch. Thin slices of beef are spread with mustard and rolled around a filling. The dish is found across Germany with regional variations in the filling.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the cooked rolls in sauce for up to 2 months.

content.text: Rinderrouladen are a German classic. Thin beef slices are rolled around a mustardy, savoury filling and braised slowly until meltingly tender. Ask your butcher to slice the beef thin for you -- it makes the rolling much easier.

items.prepNote: sliced very thin into 4 pieces -- ask butcher to slice for rouladen

content.text: Lay each beef slice flat on a board. Spread a thin layer of dijon mustard over the surface.
Lay bacon rashers, sliced onion, and capers along the centre of each slice.
Roll each slice up tightly and secure with two toothpicks or tie with kitchen string.
Heat oil in a large frying pan over high heat. Sear the rolls on all sides until browned all over, about 3-4 minutes. Remove and set aside.
Deglaze the pan with the red wine. Let it bubble for 2 minutes, scraping up any browned bits.
Add the stock and return the rolls to the pan. Cover and braise on a very low heat for 1.5 hours until very tender.
Remove the rolls and set aside. Whisk the flour with 2 tbsp cold water until smooth. Stir into the pan juices. Simmer for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens. Season and serve.

items.fix: Use two toothpicks per roll or tie with kitchen string before browning.

content.text: Rinderrouladen are a classic German Sunday lunch. Found nationwide with local variations -- some regions add pickle and carrot inside the roll. Traditionally served with red cabbage and potato dumplings.
